item.text: {"question_id":"6B.7","answer":"In 2023, Germany had formal safeguards against arbitrary allocation, including transparent preliminary housing-benefit guidance, cooperative Bürgergeld plans, hardship review, and appeal or judicial-review routes (BATCH-0022-E010; BATCH-0026-E008; BATCH-0011-R01-E003; BATCH-0011-R04-E011; BATCH-0011-R05-E012). These provisions do not establish that welfare, permits, jobs, food, or housing were broadly insulated from political favoritism or punishment. In important asylum-related domains, access remained conditional or coercive: benefits could be reduced or withdrawn, residence restrictions could affect benefits, employment was generally unavailable in reception centres and discretionary outside them, and payment-card arrangements contemplated limited cash use and blocked transfers (BATCH-0011-R04-E011; BATCH-0011-R04-E012; BATCH-0011-R04-E016; BATCH-0011-R04-E008). Family reunification for subsidiary-protection beneficiaries was discretionary and quota-based, although the quota was fulfilled in 2023 (BATCH-0011-R06-E005). Judicial remedies sometimes corrected unlawful detention and the 2023 court ruling against unlawful smartphone screening, but recurring procedural failures and limited remedy data prevent a conclusion that administrative punishment or exclusion was consistently prevented (BATCH-0011-R05-E012; BATCH-0011-R01-E016). The evidence concerns federal and subnational administration during 2023 and does not establish personal Scholz direction, nor does it directly document loyalty tests in ordinary welfare, jobs, food, or housing allocation.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0022-E010","BATCH-0026-E008","BATCH-0011-R01-E003","BATCH-0011-R04-E011","BATCH-0011-R05-E012","BATCH-0011-R01-E016"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-R04-E011","BATCH-0011-R04-E012","BATCH-0011-R04-E016","BATCH-0011-R04-E008","BATCH-0011-R06-E005","BATCH-0011-R05-E012","BATCH-0011-R01-E016"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied evidence does not directly establish political loyalty tests in ordinary welfare, jobs, food, housing, or permit allocation.","The strongest adverse evidence concerns asylum seekers and immigration administration rather than the full welfare system.","Many restrictions were established before 2023 or implemented by Länder and local authorities; personal Scholz involvement is not established.","Appeal outcomes, remedy speed, nationwide incidence, and distributional effects are incompletely measured.","Payment-card evidence concerns a 2023 decision and planned arrangement, with no established nationwide implementation or measured effect during the target year."],"corrections_made":["Removed the unsupported implication that arbitration, counselling, and judicial review demonstrated general insulation from political allocation.","Made asylum-related benefit reductions, residence restrictions, work exclusion, and payment-card limits central qualifying evidence.","Added the directly relevant residence-obligation evidence and corrected the treatment of family reunification by noting that the 2023 quota was ultimately fulfilled.","Qualified detention evidence as judicial correction alongside recurring implementation failures and non-representative or incomplete remedy data.","Restricted political-protest evidence from the answer because it concerns subnational assembly restrictions and does not directly establish welfare allocation."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Direct evidence on political favoritism or punishment in ordinary welfare, housing, food, permits, and public-sector jobs is absent from the supplied passages.","A fuller ledger could clarify whether asylum-related conditionality reflected lawful status-based administration, political punishment, or both, and could quantify actual 2023 application and appeal outcomes."]}
